expecting a direct stream of im= age pixels (like a <code data-path-to-node=3D"7" data-index-in-node=3D"65">= .jpg</code> or <code data-path-to-node=3D"7" data-index-in-node=3D"73">.png= </code>). When you give it a whole Google Drive web page instead, the brows= er gets confused, gives up, and renders it as blank.</p><hr data-path-to-no= de=3D"8"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"9">2. The "Video" Misconception</h2><p da= ta-path-to-node=3D"10">In the original code, the boxes with the play button= s weren't actually playing live videos. They were loading <b data-path-to-n= ode=3D"10" data-index-in-node=3D"110">static thumbnail images</b> pulled fr= om YouTube's image server, and I layered an SVG "play button" graphic right= on top of it to make it look like a video player.</p><p data-path-to-node= =3D"11">CSS <code data-path-to-node=3D"11" data-index-in-node=3D"4">backgro= und-image</code> can only display flat, still images. If you paste a raw vi= deo file link into a <code data-path-to-node=3D"11" data-index-in-node=3D"1= 00">background-image</code> property, it won=E2=80=99t play; it will just s= how up blank.</p><hr data-path-to-node=3D"12"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"13">= How to Fix It Easily</h2><p data-path-to-node=3D"14">You have two great opt= ions to get your visuals showing up perfectly:</p><h3 data-path-to-node=3D"= 15">Option A: Convert your Drive links into "Direct" links (Easiest)</h3><p= data-path-to-node=3D"16">You can manually convert your Google Drive share = links into direct image links that the code can read.</p><ol start=3D"1" da= ta-path-to-node=3D"17"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"17,0,0">Look at your Goo= gle Drive share link and copy the long string of random letters and numbers= in the middle. This is your <b data-path-to-node=3D"17,0,0" data-index-in-= node=3D"120">File ID</b>:</p></li></ol><blockquote data-path-to-node=3D"18"= ><p data-path-to-node=3D"18,0"><code data-path-to-node=3D"18,0" data-index-= in-node=3D"0">[https://drive.google.com/file/d/](https://drive.google.com/f= ile/d/)</code><b data-path-to-node=3D"18,0" data-index-in-node=3D"68">1A2B3= C4D5E6F_YOUR_FILE_ID</b><code data-path-to-node=3D"18,0" data-index-in-node= =3D"93">/view?usp=3Dsharing</code></p></blockquote><ol start=3D"2" data-pat= h-to-node=3D"19"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"19,0,0">Swap that ID into this= exact URL structure:</p></li></ol><blockquote data-path-to-node=3D"20"><p = data-path-to-node=3D"20,0"><code data-path-to-node=3D"20,0" data-index-in-n= ode=3D"0">[https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/d/](https://lh3.googleusercont= ent.com/d/)</code><b data-path-to-node=3D"20,0" data-index-in-node=3D"76">1= A2B3C4D5E6F_YOUR_FILE_ID</b></p></blockquote><p data-path-to-node=3D"21">Us= e this new link inside your <code data-path-to-node=3D"21" data-index-in-no= de=3D"30">url('...')</code> code, and the image will pop right up!</p><h3 d= ata-path-to-node=3D"22">Option B: Use a Dedicated Image Host (Highly Recomm= ended)</h3><p data-path-to-node=3D"23">While the Drive trick works, Google = Drive can sometimes be slow to load or temporarily block images if your por= tfolio gets a lot of traffic.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"24">As a professio= nal setup, it's usually much better to upload your project screenshots to a= free, fast image hosting site like <b data-path-to-node=3D"24" data-index-= in-node=3D"125">Imgur</b> or <b data-path-to-node=3D"24" data-index-in-node= =3D"134">Postimages</b>. Once uploaded, right-click the image, select <b da= ta-path-to-node=3D"24" data-index-in-node=3D"191">"Copy Image Address"</b> = (making sure it ends in <code data-path-to-node=3D"24" data-index-in-node= =3D"236">.jpg</code> or <code data-path-to-node=3D"24" data-index-in-node= =3D"244">.png</code>), and paste <i data-path-to-node=3D"24" data-index-in-= node=3D"261">that</i> into your code.</p><hr data-path-to-node=3D"25"><p da= ta-path-to-node=3D"26">Are you planning to have these project cards eventua= lly open up a pop-up video player, or would you prefer to keep them as clea= n, static image links that redirect clients somewhere else?</p></div></mess= age-content><!----></div></structured-content-container><!----><!----><!---= -><div _ngcontent-ng-c1364954901=3D"" style=3D"--animation-duration: 400ms; --fade-anima= tion-function: ease-out;"><p data-path-to-node=3D"0">Yes, you can absolutel= y upload your HTML file, images, and folders directly to GitHub! And don't = worry=E2=80=94GitHub didn't break, your free plan isn't maxed out (GitHub a= ctually allows unlimited public and private repositories on the free plan),= and making it public didn't cause this.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"1">What= you are looking at is GitHub's standard "empty repository" landing page. I= t looks intimidating because it defaults to showing developer command-line = instructions, but you can bypass all of that and use your browser.</p><p da= ta-path-to-node=3D"2">Here is exactly what's happening and how to fix it.</= p><hr data-path-to-node=3D"3"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"4">1. Why the "creat= e a new file" link isn't working</h2><p data-path-to-node=3D"5">When a repo= sitory is completely empty, GitHub shows a screen filled with code setups. = Sometimes, clicking the tiny "create a new file" text link on that initial = quick-setup page fails because the repository doesn't have a <b data-path-t= o-node=3D"5" data-index-in-node=3D"222">default branch</b> (like <code data= -path-to-node=3D"5" data-index-in-node=3D"243">main</code>) initialized yet= .</p><h3 data-path-to-node=3D"6">The Easiest Web Fix (No Code Required):</h= 3><p data-path-to-node=3D"7">Look at the very top of that page for a sectio= n called <b data-path-to-node=3D"7" data-index-in-node=3D"55">Quick setup</= b>. Right next to it, you'll see a button that says <b data-path-to-node=3D= "7" data-index-in-node=3D"116">"creating a new file"</b> or a button to <b = data-path-to-node=3D"7" data-index-in-node=3D"153">"uploading an existing f= ile"</b>.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"8">If those are giving you trouble, do= this to force the repository to initialize:</p><ol start=3D"1" data-path-t= o-node=3D"9"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,0,0">Scroll down to the bottom o= f that page.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,1,0">Look for an option = to add a <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"28">README.md= </b> file or click <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"52"= >Initialize this repository with a README</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-= node=3D"9,2,0">Once you hit "Commit" or "Create," your repository will inst= antly change from a scary code page into a clean, visual folder structure.<= /p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0">Once initialized, a prominent <b= data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0" data-index-in-node=3D"30">Add file</b> button = will appear at the top right of your repository page, allowing you to simpl= y <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0" data-index-in-node=3D"123">Drag and Drop</= b> your HTML file and image files right from your computer desktop.</p></li= ></ol><hr data-path-to-node=3D"10"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"11">2. Breaking= Down the Command Line Instructions (In Detail)</h2><p data-path-to-node=3D= "12">If you <i data-path-to-node=3D"12" data-index-in-node=3D"7">do</i> wan= t to understand what those terminal commands mean, they are instructions fo= r <b data-path-to-node=3D"12" data-index-in-node=3D"90">Git</b>, a software= tool that tracks changes in code. Developers use their computer's terminal= /command prompt to send files to GitHub instead of using a web browser.</p>= <p data-path-to-node=3D"13">Here is a line-by-line translation of exactly w= hat those commands are doing:</p><h3 data-path-to-node=3D"14">Section A: Cr= eate a new repository from scratch</h3><p data-path-to-node=3D"15">If you h= ave a folder on your computer with your website code and want to link it to= GitHub using your terminal:</p><ul data-path-to-node=3D"16"><li><p data-pa= th-to-node=3D"16,0,0"><code data-path-to-node=3D"16,0,0" data-index-in-node= =3D"0">echo "# systems-ops-portfolio" >> README.md</code></p><ul data= -path-to-node=3D"16,0,1"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,0,1,0,0"><b data-pa= th-to-node=3D"16,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">What it means:</b> This = creates a text file named <code data-path-to-node=3D"16,0,1,0,0" data-index= -in-node=3D"46">README.md</code> on your computer and writes the headline <= code data-path-to-node=3D"16,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"97"># systems-o= ps-portfolio</code> inside it. It ensures your project isn't empty.</p></li= ></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,1,0"><code data-path-to-node=3D"1= 6,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">git init</code></p><ul data-path-to-node=3D= "16,1,1"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,1,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-node=3D"16= ,1,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">What it means:</b> "Initialize Git." Thi= s tells your computer to start tracking this specific local folder as a cod= ing project. It creates a hidden tracking folder.</p></li></ul></li><li><p = data-path-to-node=3D"16,2,0"><code data-path-to-node=3D"16,2,0" data-index-= in-node=3D"0">git add README.md</code></p><ul data-path-to-node=3D"16,2,1">= <li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,2,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-node=3D"16,2,1,0,0"= data-index-in-node=3D"0">What it means:</b> This stages the file, telling = Git: <i data-path-to-node=3D"16,2,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"50">"Hey, pr= epare this README file to be sent to the internet on my next trip."</i></p>= </li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,3,0"><code data-path-to-node= =3D"16,3,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">git commit -m "first commit"</code></p= ><ul data-path-to-node=3D"16,3,1"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,3,1,0,0"><= b data-path-to-node=3D"16,3,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">What it means:<= /b> This takes a permanent snapshot of your staged files on your local comp= uter. The <code data-path-to-node=3D"16,3,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"96">= -m "first commit"</code> is just a label or log note describing what change= d in this snapshot.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,4,0"><= code data-path-to-node=3D"16,4,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">git branch -M ma= in</code></p><ul data-path-to-node=3D"16,4,1"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"1= 6,4,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-node=3D"16,4,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">Wha= t it means:</b> This ensures your primary development timeline (or branch) = is explicitly named <code data-path-to-node=3D"16,4,1,0,0" data-index-in-no= de=3D"94">main</code>.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,5,0= "><code data-path-to-node=3D"16,5,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">git remote ad= d origin [https://github.com/CreativeCo/systems-ops-portfolio.git](https://= github.com/CreativeCo/systems-ops-portfolio.git)</code></p><ul data-path-to= -node=3D"16,5,1"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,5,1,0,0"><b data-path-to-no= de=3D"16,5,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">What it means:</b> This links yo= ur local computer folder to your specific GitHub account online. It sets yo= ur online repository URL as the primary destination, nicknamed <code data-p= ath-to-node=3D"16,5,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"166">origin</code>.</p></l= i></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,6,0"><code data-path-to-node=3D"= 16,6,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">git push -u origin main</code></p><ul data= -path-to-node=3D"16,6,1"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"16,6,1,0,0"><b data-pa= th-to-node=3D"16,6,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">What it means:</b> This = is the actual execution command. It takes the snapshot you committed locall= y and "pushes" (uploads) it over the internet to your online GitHub reposit= ory's <code data-path-to-node=3D"16,6,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"176">mai= n</code> branch.</p></li></ul></li></ul><h3 data-path-to-node=3D"17">Sectio= n B: Push an existing repository</h3><p data-path-to-node=3D"18">If you had= <i data-path-to-node=3D"18" data-index-in-node=3D"11">already</i> run <cod= e data-path-to-node=3D"18" data-index-in-node=3D"23">git init</code> on you= r computer weeks ago and had a history of commits saved locally, you wouldn= 't need to create a new README file or initialize it again. You would only = run these final three lines:</p><ol start=3D"1" data-path-to-node=3D"19"><l= i><p data-path-to-node=3D"19,0,0">Link your folder to the online URL (<code= data-path-to-node=3D"19,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"36">git remote add...</= code>).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"19,1,0">Name the branch <code d= ata-path-to-node=3D"19,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"16">main</code> (<code da= ta-path-to-node=3D"19,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"22">git branch -M...</code= >).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"19,2,0">Upload the data (<code data= -path-to-node=3D"19,2,0" data-index-in-node=3D"17">git push...</code>).</p>= </li></ol><hr data-path-to-node=3D"20"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"21">Which m= ethod should you use?</h2><p data-path-to-node=3D"22">For now, stick to the= <b data-path-to-node=3D"22" data-index-in-node=3D"22">Web Browser method</= b>.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"23">Go back to your GitHub repository page, = look for the option to <b data-path-to-node=3D"23" data-index-in-node=3D"63= ">initialize with a README file</b> to clear that default placeholder scree= n, and then use the clean interface to drag, drop, and commit your HTML fil= e and your images folder. ain-panel tutor-markdown-rendering stronger enable-updated-hr-color" id=3D"= model-response-message-contentr_92e562d9588f42a3" aria-live=3D"off" aria-bu= sy=3D"false" dir=3D"ltr" style=3D"--animation-duration: 400ms; --fade-anima= tion-function: ease-out;"><p data-path-to-node=3D"0">Ah, that explains it p= erfectly! You are getting caught in a classic "chicken-and-egg" loop that h= appens with brand new GitHub repositories.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"1">Be= cause the repository is completely empty, it technically doesn't have a sin= gle "branch" (a timeline) created yet. When you click <b data-path-to-node= =3D"1" data-index-in-node=3D"131">"uploading an existing file"</b>, GitHub = tries to drop your files into a branch that doesn't exist, freaks out, and = gives you that error message.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"2">Since the web l= inks on that empty landing page are acting frozen, we need to manually forc= e GitHub to create its very first branch (<code data-path-to-node=3D"2" dat= a-index-in-node=3D"132">main</code>). Once we do that, the drag-and-drop fi= le uploader will instantly unlock.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"3">Here is th= e exact, bulletproof way to fix this directly in your browser:</p><hr data-= path-to-node=3D"4"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"5">The 60-Second Fix to Unlock = Uploads</h2><ol start=3D"1" data-path-to-node=3D"6"><li><p data-path-to-nod= e=3D"6,0,0">Go to your repository main page (the one with all the code comm= ands).</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"6,1,0">Look <i data-path-to-node= =3D"6,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"5">just above</i> that first block of code= instructions. You will see a small section titled: <b data-path-to-node=3D"6,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"92">"Quick setup =E2= =80=94 if you=E2=80=99ve done this kind of thing before"</b></p></li><li><p= data-path-to-node=3D"6,2,0">In that row, look all the way to the right. Yo= u will see two small buttons: <b data-path-to-node=3D"6,2,0" data-index-in-= node=3D"76">HTTPS</b> and <b data-path-to-node=3D"6,2,0" data-index-in-node= =3D"86">SSH</b>. Right next to them, look for a button that says <b data-pa= th-to-node=3D"6,2,0" data-index-in-node=3D"139">Add file</b> or a checkbox/= button to <b data-path-to-node=3D"6,2,0" data-index-in-node=3D"172">Initial= ize this repository with a README</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"= 6,3,0"><b data-path-to-node=3D"6,3,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">If you don't= see that:</b> Look at the very top right of the page for your repository s= ettings or look at the bottom of the page.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node= =3D"6,4,0"><b data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">The ulti= mate shortcut:</b> If the page links are completely locked up, look at the = very center of the page where it says: <code data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,0" data-index-in-node=3D"118">echo "# system= s-ops-portfolio" >> README.md</code></p><p data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,1= ">Instead of using the command line, we can just click the <b data-path-to-= node=3D"6,4,1" data-index-in-node=3D"57">"create a new file"</b> blue text = link right next to it.</p><ul data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,2"><li><p data-path-= to-node=3D"6,4,2,0,0"><i data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,2,0,0" data-index-in-node= =3D"0">If that link is also frozen:</i> Change the URL in your browser's ad= dress bar. At the end of your repository URL, add <code data-path-to-node= =3D"6,4,2,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"114">/new/main</code> so it looks like= this: <code data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,2,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"147">[https://g= ithub.com/CreativeCo/systems-ops-portfolio/new/main](https://github.com/Cre= ativeCo/systems-ops-portfolio/new/main)</code></p></li><li><p data-path-to-= node=3D"6,4,2,1,0">Hit Enter. This forces GitHub to open the "New File" scr= een on a brand new branch named <code data-path-to-node=3D"6,4,2,1,0" data-= index-in-node=3D"88">main</code>.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-nod= e=3D"6,5,0">On this new file screen:</p><ul data-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1"><li= ><p data-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1,0,0">Name the file: <code data-path-to-node= =3D"6,5,1,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"15">README.md</code></p></li><li><p da= ta-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1,1,0">In the big text box below, just type: <code d= ata-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"38"># Systems Portfoli= o</code></p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1,2,0">Scroll down to the = bottom and click the green <b data-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1,2,0" data-index-in= -node=3D"46">Commit changes</b> (or <b data-path-to-node=3D"6,5,1,2,0" data= -index-in-node=3D"65">Create file</b>) button.</p></li></ul></li></ol><hr d= ata-path-to-node=3D"7"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"8">What Happens Next?</h2><= p data-path-to-node=3D"9">The moment you click that green button, your repo= sitory is officially born. The scary page with all the command-line code wi= ll completely disappear.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"10">Instead, you will s= ee a clean, professional file directory screen displaying your new <code da= ta-path-to-node=3D"10" data-index-in-node=3D"86">README.md</code> file.</p>= <p data-path-to-node=3D"11">More importantly, a prominent, fully functional= <b data-path-to-node=3D"11" data-index-in-node=3D"48">Add file</b> button = will now be waiting for you at the top right of the screen. You can click i= t, select <b data-path-to-node=3D"11" data-index-in-node=3D"149">Upload fil= es</b>, and drag your HTML file and your images folder straight into GitHub= with zero errors!</p></div></message-content><!----></div></structured-con= tent-container><!----><!----><!----><div _ngcontent-ng-c1364954901=3D"" cla= ss=3D"response-footer gap complete data-path-to-node=3D"0">No, you absol= utely do not have to use that other repository if you don't want to!</p><p = data-path-to-node=3D"1">Since you already have a repository that has a <cod= e data-path-to-node=3D"1" data-index-in-node=3D"47">main</code> branch init= ialized, it is completely up to your personal preference. You have two perf= ectly fine choices right now:</p><h3 data-path-to-node=3D"2">Choice 1: Use = the other repository (Easiest)</h3><p data-path-to-node=3D"3">If you want t= o save yourself a few clicks, just open up that other repository that alrea= dy has the <code data-path-to-node=3D"3" data-index-in-node=3D"99">main</co= de> branch. Because it's already initialized, you will immediately see that= glorious, fully functional <b data-path-to-node=3D"3" data-index-in-node= =3D"203">Add file</b> button at the top right. You can click it, select <b = data-path-to-node=3D"3" data-index-in-node=3D"262">Upload files</b>, drag y= our files in, and you're good to go.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"4">If you d= on't like the name of that repository, you can easily change it:</p><ol sta= rt=3D"1" data-path-to-node=3D"5"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"5,0,0">Click t= he <b data-path-to-node=3D"5,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"10">Settings</b> ta= b (the gear icon at the top of that repository).</p></li><li><p data-path-t= o-node=3D"5,1,0">Right at the very top, change the name under "Repository n= ame" and click <b data-path-to-node=3D"5,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"73">Ren= ame</b>.</p></li></ol><h3 data-path-to-node=3D"6">Choice 2: Stick with the = current one (<code data-path-to-node=3D"6" data-index-in-node=3D"38">system= s-ops-portfolio</code>)</h3><p data-path-to-node=3D"7">If you prefer to kee= p using the current repository you've been looking at, you just need to get= past that empty placeholder page by forcing it to create its first file.</= p><p data-path-to-node=3D"8">If the links on that page are completely froze= n and refusing to let you click them, you can bypass the interface entirely= using your browser's address bar:</p><ol start=3D"1" data-path-to-node=3D"= 9"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,0,0">Look at your browser's URL box. It sh= ould currently say: <code data-path-to-node=3D"9,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"57">[https://github= .com/CreativeCo/systems-ops-portfolio](https://github.com/CreativeCo/system= s-ops-portfolio)</code></p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,1,0">Erase th= at, type this exact URL instead, and hit enter: <code data-path-to-node=3D"9,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"56">[https://github= .com/CreativeCo/systems-ops-portfolio/new/main](https://github.com/Creative= Co/systems-ops-portfolio/new/main)</code></p></li><li><p data-path-to-node= =3D"9,2,0">This forces GitHub to skip the broken screen and opens a blank "= Create New File" page.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0">Type <cod= e data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0" data-index-in-node=3D"5">README.md</code> as = the filename, type anything you want in the big box below it, and scroll do= wn to click the green <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0" data-index-in-node=3D"= 115">Commit changes</b> button.</p></li></ol><p data-path-to-node=3D"10">Th= e moment you do that, this repository will lock into place, the command-lin= e text will vanish, and the file uploader will unlock for you! Let me know = which route you decide to take.</p></div></message-content><!----></div></s= tructured-content-container><!----><!----><!----><div _ngcontent-ng-c136495= 4901=3D"" You beat the system.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"1">Now that you= are inside a fully initialized repository, you are ready to upload your fi= les and turn this into a real, live website. Here are your next steps:</p><= hr data-path-to-node=3D"2"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"3">Step 1: Upload Your = Website Files</h2><ol start=3D"1" data-path-to-node=3D"4"><li><p data-path-= to-node=3D"4,0,0">On your main repository page, click the <b data-path-to-n= ode=3D"4,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"40">Add file</b> button near the top ri= ght and select <b data-path-to-node=3D"4,0,0" data-index-in-node=3D"86">Upl= oad files</b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"4,1,0"><b data-path-to-n= ode=3D"4,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"0">Drag and drop</b> your portfolio HTM= L file directly into the upload area.</p><ul data-path-to-node=3D"4,1,1"><l= i><p data-path-to-node=3D"4,1,1,0,0"><i data-path-to-node=3D"4,1,1,0,0" dat= a-index-in-node=3D"0">Note:</i> For a website to work seamlessly on GitHub,= your main HTML file <b data-path-to-node=3D"4,1,1,0,0" data-index-in-node= =3D"70">must</b> be named exactly <code data-path-to-node=3D"4,1,1,0,0" dat= a-index-in-node=3D"92">index.html</code> (all lowercase). If it's named som= ething else on your computer, rename it now before uploading.</p></li></ul>= </li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"4,2,0">If you have an images folder on you= r computer for your project screenshots, drag that entire folder into the u= pload box as well.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"4,3,0">Scroll down t= o the bottom of the page and click the green <b data-path-to-node=3D"4,3,0"= data-index-in-node=3D"58">Commit changes</b> button.</p></li></ol><p data-= path-to-node=3D"5">GitHub will take a few seconds to process the upload, an= d you'll see your files sitting neatly next to your <code data-path-to-node= =3D"5" data-index-in-node=3D"108">README.md</code>.</p><hr data-path-to-nod= e=3D"6"><h2 data-path-to-node=3D"7">Step 2: Launch the Website Live (Free H= osting)</h2><p data-path-to-node=3D"8">GitHub comes with a built-in feature= called <b data-path-to-node=3D"8" data-index-in-node=3D"44">GitHub Pages</= b> that will host your portfolio on the internet for free. Let's turn it on= :</p><ol start=3D"1" data-path-to-node=3D"9"><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,= 0,0">At the top of your repository, look at the menu tabs (Code, Issues, Pu= ll Requests...) and click on the <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,0,0" data-index-= in-node=3D"103">Settings</b> gear icon.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D= "9,1,0">In the left-hand sidebar, scroll down to the <b data-path-to-node= =3D"9,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"45">Code and automation</b> section and cl= ick on <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,1,0" data-index-in-node=3D"86">Pages</b>.<= /p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,2,0">Under the <b data-path-to-node= =3D"9,2,0" data-index-in-node=3D"10">Build and deployment</b> section, look= for <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,2,0" data-index-in-node=3D"49">Source</b>. I= t should default to "Deploy from a branch".</p></li><li><p data-path-to-nod= e=3D"9,3,0">Right below that, under <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0" data-ind= ex-in-node=3D"24">Branch</b>, change it from <code data-path-to-node=3D"9,3= ,0" data-index-in-node=3D"47">None</code> to <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0"= data-index-in-node=3D"55"><code data-path-to-node=3D"9,3,0" data-index-in-= node=3D"55">main</code></b>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node=3D"9,4,0">Lea= ve the folder dropdown right next to it set to <code data-path-to-node=3D"9= ,4,0" data-index-in-node=3D"50">/ (root)</code>.</p></li><li><p data-path-t= o-node=3D"9,5,0">Click the <b data-path-to-node=3D"9,5,0" data-index-in-nod= e=3D"10">Save</b> button.</p></li></ol><hr data-path-to-node=3D"10"><h2 dat= a-path-to-node=3D"11">Step 3: View Your Live Portfolio</h2><p data-path-to-= node=3D"12">Give GitHub about 30 to 60 seconds to build your site in the ba= ckground.</p><p data-path-to-node=3D"13">Refresh your page, and at the very= top of that same <b data-path-to-node=3D"13" data-index-in-node=3D"52">Set= tings -> Pages</b> screen, a box will appear saying: <b data-path-to-nod= e=3D"13" data-index-in-node=3D"104">"Your site is live at..."</b> followed = by a URL (usually looking like <code data-path-to-node=3D"13" data-index-in= -node=3D"170">[https://yourusername.github.io/your-repository-name/](https:= //yourusername.github.io/your-repository-name/)</code>).</p><p data-path-to= -node=3D"14">Click that link, and your portfolio=E2=80=94spotlight effect, = dynamic background, and all=E2=80=94is officially live on the internet! Let= me know if everything loads up beautifully.</p></div></message-content><!-= ---></div></structured-content-container><!----><!----><!----><div _ngconte= nt-ng-c1364954901=3D""
